title: A diver for the lake, not the boardroom
quote: I wanted one watch I could swim in, travel with and still wear to dinner. OUDYN found it, serviced it and told me exactly what had been replaced.
excerpt: Andrea came in looking for a tool, not a trophy. The UNO 40 left the studio with a fresh service and a strap drawn for the lake.
body: Andrea had been looking for a diver for almost a year. Most of what he found online was either too polished to wear in the water or too fragile to wear anywhere else. He wanted a watch with a real bezel, a readable dial and a service history he could hold in his hand.

The UNO 40 we sourced came from a private collection in Monza. The case was strong, the bezel still clicked cleanly, and the movement was running inside specification but had never been serviced. We stripped it, cleaned it, replaced the gaskets and timed it in six positions before it went back on the wrist.

Andrea chose a black TPU strap for the lake and a gray NATO for the city. Before he left, we photographed the watch, the caseback and the timing sheet. The authentication report and the two-year warranty went into the travel case with it.
Six months later he sent us a photograph from the shore of Lake Como. The watch was wet, the bezel was still at twelve, and the dial was as legible as the day he collected it.

title: The first good watch
quote: It is the first watch I have owned that does not make me feel like I am wearing someone else's idea of a woman's watch.
excerpt: A 36 mm time-only watch, bought for a first promotion and worn every day since. Giulia wanted a quiet dial and a case that would survive real life.
body: Giulia came to the studio with a photograph of her grandmother's watch and a clear brief: 36 mm, a pale dial, no diamonds, no compromise on the movement. She had spent months looking at new watches and found most of them either too small or too decorative.

The DUE 36 we found was a 2022 example with a matte white dial and a steel case that had been worn gently. The bracelet was short, so we added two links from our parts drawer and regulated the movement before delivery.
She chose it because the dial is quiet enough to read at a glance. The case has enough presence to wear with a suit, and the automatic movement means she never has to think about a battery.
The watch now travels between Torino and Brussels. Giulia sends us a note every few months, usually about a new strap or a scratch she has decided to keep.

title: Inherited, then restored properly
quote: They did not try to make it look new. They made it work again and told me what to keep.
excerpt: A family watch with a cloudy crystal and a stopped movement. The brief was simple: keep the history, make it wearable.
body: Sofia brought in a watch that had belonged to her father. It had been in a drawer for eleven years, the crystal was cloudy, the crown was stiff and the movement would run for a few hours and stop.

We opened it, photographed every component and sent her a written estimate before touching anything. The movement needed a full service; the crystal was replaced with a correct-profile sapphire; the original crown was kept because the threads were still sound.

She asked us not to polish the case. The small marks on the lugs are part of the watch's history, and a heavy polish would have softened the case lines. We cleaned it, replaced the gaskets and left the rest alone.
The watch now runs within eight seconds a day. Sofia wears it on a gray suede strap and keeps the original box, papers and our service report together in the travel case.

title: A Tokyo trade, handled in Milano
quote: I needed a GMT I could trust from a dealer I had never met. The photographs, the timing sheet and the video call made the decision easy.
excerpt: A long-distance purchase with no showroom visit. Kenji bought the CINQUE GMT from Tokyo after a 40-minute video inspection.
body: Kenji had been following the studio for a year. He wanted a GMT for frequent trips between Tokyo and Europe, but he was not willing to buy without seeing the actual watch.

We booked a video inspection: case, lugs, bezel, dial, hands, crown, caseback and bracelet, all under a macro lens. We ran the movement on the timing machine while he watched and sent the printout with the invoice.

The watch shipped insured and signature-required. It arrived in Tokyo four working days later, still on the temporary strap we had fitted for transit. The original bracelet travelled separately in the case.
His only complaint was the time difference during the call. We now schedule inspections in the morning Milan time, which is late afternoon in Tokyo.

images.alt: GMT watch worn on the wrist

title: The collector who traded down
quote: I owned twelve watches. I now own three, and I wear this one more than the other two combined.
excerpt: Elias traded two modern pieces for one older field watch and a smaller collection. The deal was agreed over three weeks and a shared spreadsheet.
body: Elias had a collection built around completeness: every colourway, every bracelet, every box. Somewhere in the middle of it he stopped wearing any of them.

He proposed a trade: two modern references against one SEI FIELD and a cash balance. We valued both sides against recent sales, not asking prices, and put the numbers in writing before anything shipped.

The SEI FIELD was a 2023 example with a cream dial and a case that had seen real use. We serviced it, fitted a new crystal and left the case unpolished. Elias wanted a watch he could wear without thinking about resale value.
He now keeps a three-watch collection: the SEI FIELD, a dress watch from his father and one chronograph. The spreadsheet is gone.

title: A wedding watch with a past
quote: We wanted something old enough to have a story, but solid enough to wear for the next forty years.
excerpt: A couple bought a chronograph instead of matching new watches. The caseback is engraved with the date, and the original parts stay in the box.
body: Léa and Thomas came to Milano for a weekend and left with a plan. They wanted one watch between them rather than two new ones, and they wanted it to mark the wedding without looking like a gift-shop engraving.

The SETTE CHRONO was a 2018 full-set example with a panda dial. The case had been worn, the pushers were crisp, and the service history was complete. We serviced it and replaced the gaskets before the engraving.
The caseback carries their wedding date in a small, single line. The original caseback is kept untouched in the box, so the watch can return to its original specification later.
They alternate wearing it. Thomas takes it on work trips; Léa wears it with a black leather strap on weekends. The original bracelet stays in the case for winter.
